reimbursement_policies.evidence: The policy is on-topic for obstetric vaginal delivery claims but does not adjudicate by DRG or state a Texas-specific acuity/CC payment rule. Instead, it reimburses professional obstetric services using global versus component billing rules. Single vaginal delivery is reimbursed at 100% of the maximum allowance when the appropriate global, delivery-only, or delivery/postpartum code is reported. Routine antepartum, delivery, postpartum, and pregnancy-related E/M services are bundled into the global obstetric package when the same provider or provider group under the same TIN furnishes all components. Additional vaginal deliveries require modifier 59 and are reduced to 50%. Duplicate or overlapping pregnancy services and several labor-management services are not separately reimbursed.

Ohio and Virginia: more than two maternity ultrasounds per pregnancy/fetus per patient are not eligible for separate reimbursement unless related to a problem oriented diagnosis

reimbursement_policies.evidence: Routine vaginal delivery is bundled into the global OB maternity package when antepartum, delivery, and postpartum care are provided by the same qualified professional or same location/TIN. Complications of pregnancy or surgical complications are separately reportable with appropriate CPT/HCPCS/E/M codes when documented.

The policy is on-topic for maternity professional billing but does not provide inpatient DRG/MS-DRG payment logic or separate severity rules for CC, sterilization, or D&C. For vaginal delivery claims, routine antepartum, delivery, and postpartum services are reimbursed as a single global package after delivery when the same clinician or group provides all components; pregnancy-complication E&M may be separately payable only under stated conditions.

reimbursement_policies.evidence: This policy governs multiple-birth maternity delivery claims using CPT and ICD-10 codes rather than DRG codes. When a multiple gestation diagnosis is reported and at least one delivery is vaginal, the primary delivery is reimbursed at 100% and each secondary delivery at 50%. All-cesarean multiple births are not typically paid extra unless modifier 22 is supported by substantially increased time and complexity.
Commercial policy for multiple delivery services applies to vaginal deliveries in multiple births. Subsequent vaginal deliveries are reimbursed at 50% of the allowance when billed with Modifier 59.

Moda Health's maternity policy bundles management of complications that occur during vaginal delivery into the delivery service/global OB package. Intrapartum complication management is not separately reimbursable; separately identifiable services outside the global package may be paid, and related post-delivery return-to-OR surgical care may be separately considered with modifier 78.

Routine vaginal-delivery-related services are included in the maternity package and do not justify extra reimbursement under modifier 22; modifier 22 is denied for facility claims and is only considered in very unusual maternity cases with documented extra difficulty.

The policy is not DRG-specific, but it governs Texas obstetrical delivery billing for vaginal deliveries and related complications. In Texas, global OB codes are not reimbursed, delivery and postpartum services are billed separately, and third- or fourth-degree laceration repairs may support modifier 22 on delivery codes. Routine delivery components are bundled into the delivery code.

recommended_action.description:
Recommendation 1: Bundle routine antepartum and postpartum into 59510, 59514, 59515, and 59618 when billed under the same TIN and on the same claim; allow 59425, 59426, or 59430 only when antepartum not rendered, postpartum not rendered, or 1-3 antepartum visits billed separately, and send claims above approximately 13 prenatal visits / more than 13 antepartum visits to exception review. Exempt: appropriate E&M for 1-3 antepartum visits. Peer: BCBS TX, Cigna, Moda, and United all manage maternity package codes such as 59400/59510/59618 within global-OB policy logic, with same-TIN and same-claim bundling used by peers..

Recommendation 2: For multiple-birth cesarean claims, require modifier 22 on 59510 or 59618, reimburse the primary at 100% and the secondary at 50%, and route any enhanced payment request through same claim line review with written appeal; reserve this pathway for documented complex cesarean cases. Exempt: modifier 22 for complex cesarean, cesarean multiple gestation. Peer: Cigna requires modifier 22 and pays the secondary delivery at 50% in multiple births, while Moda separately reviews modifier 22 requests on 59510 and 59618..

Recommendation 3: Do not bundle complication care into 59510, 59514, 59515, or 59618 when the claim supports modifier 25 for current complication E&M or documents surgical complications or medical complications of pregnancy; separately reportable ancillary services should remain payable outside the routine OB package. Exempt: current complication E&M, surgical complications, medical complications of pregnancy, separately reportable ancillary services. Peer: BCBS TX and Cigna both carve complication services out of maternity-package bundling, and Cigna specifically preserves modifier 25 current-complication E&M..
